notes: Built from the 500 BCE map, adjusted to 550.

Before Cyrus the Great: Media held Iran, Armenia and Anatolia east of the Halys, with Persis (Anshan) as its vassal; Lydia under Croesus held Anatolia west of the Halys; the Neo-Babylonian Empire of Nabonidus held Mesopotamia, Syria and the Levant; Egypt under Amasis II held Cyprus.
Cyrus overthrew Media in 550–549 and took Lydia (c. 547) and Babylon (539); Cambyses took Egypt in 525.
Rome was still ruled by kings; the Republic dates from 509.
Northern India was divided among the Mahajanapadas.
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Northern Europe is in the Iron Age by this date (the Jastorf culture and its neighbours).
The Urnfield cultures ended about 750 BCE: central Europe is Hallstatt, then the Celts of the La Tène culture.
The Hallstatt culture ended about 450 BCE: central Europe is the Celts of the La Tène culture, with the Germanic peoples to the north, and later the Germanic tribes.
The Pontic steppe is the Scythians, then the Sarmatians; the Cimmerians are gone by about 600 BCE.
Between the Oder and the Vistula, Bronze Age culture names give way to the Przeworsk and Wielbark cultures, the Germanic tribes and the Slavs.
The Karasuk culture ended about 800 BCE: the Kazakh steppe is the Saka (Scythian) nomads, then the Saka and Wusun.
Mongolia is named for its peoples and cultures of the time, not for the disputed "Proto-Altaic" language theory; after the Xiongnu, the Xianbei.
China's northern frontier was the land of the Rong and Di, later the Wuhuan; Thai peoples lived far to the south.
The Caribbean islands were settled from about 5000 BCE (the Bahamas from about 700 CE): Archaic peoples, then the Saladoid peoples and the Taíno.
Andean and Amazonian peoples are named for their time.
North American cultures are named for their time; the Mississippi and Ohio valleys were the land of the Mississippian and Fort Ancient cultures (boxes approximate).
Central Asia and the forest-steppe are named for their peoples of the time; the Tarim Basin was a land of oasis city-states (lines approximate).
